ground_truth.description: The set_task_status verification rule says to increment the success counter (e.g. tasks_reopened) whenever newStatus matches the requested status. A no-op call (task already in the requested status) has newStatus == requested, so it is over-counted as a successful operation. The later-corrected version explicitly added a `"no_op": true` branch that skips the increment, confirming this omission over-reports counters and defeats the task's goal of verifying real operation success.

The guidance counts status="combined" toward tasks_created, but a combined ticket was merged into an existing task (no new task created, per lines 41-42), so incrementing tasks_created inflates the creation count.

The set_task_status response contract is described only as a single per-task record (tasks[n] with camelCase taskId/oldStatus/newStatus) and omits the comma-separated-list wrapper ({"success": bool, "results": [...]}) and per-id result.error cases. An agent applying the top-level newStatus rule to a batched call, or encountering a per-id error, will mis-count or spuriously flag/escalate a discrepancy — consistent with the review-passed-but-escalation-created symptom. Field naming is also inconsistent (taskId camelCase vs task_id snake_case used elsewhere).

task.title: Fix reconciliation agents to verify operation success before incrementing stat counters
task.description: Both Stage 1 (memory_consolidator) and Stage 2 (task_knowledge_sync) reconciliation agents prematurely increment success counters without verifying the underlying operation actually succeeded, inflating reported stats. Stage 1 inflates memories_written by counting every add_memory call attempt regardless of whether Mem0 wrote anything (empty memory_ids = deduplication/filter = no-op). Stage 2 inflates tasks_reopened and tasks_created before confirming that add_task or set_task_status actually took effect (silent failures from deduplication, network error, or timeout go undetected). Fix both stages so counters only advance on confirmed success.
task.details:
**Stage 1 fix — memory_consolidator (skills/memory-consolidator.md or equivalent):**
- After each `add_memory(...)` call, inspect the returned `memory_ids` list.
- Pattern: `if add_memory(...)['memory_ids']: memories_written += 1`
- An empty list means Mem0 deduplicated or filtered the write — count as a no-op, not a successful addition.
- Per CLAUDE.md guidance: 'After calling add_memory, inspect the memory_ids field in the response. An empty list means Mem0 deduplicated or filtered the write and no new memory was created — count it as a no-op, not a successful addition.'

**Stage 2 fix — task_knowledge_sync agent prompt/code:**
- After each `add_task` or `set_task_status` call, call `get_task` with the returned task_id to confirm the task exists and has the expected status.
- Only then increment `tasks_created` or `tasks_reopened`.
- If the returned task_id is missing or `get_task` returns an unexpected status, skip the counter increment and log the discrepancy.

**Scope:** Stage 1 and Stage 2 reporting loops in the reconciliation agent prompts/skills (fused-memory reconciliation skills directory or equivalent markdown skill files).

**FILES_TO_MODIFY:**
  - skills/memory-consolidator.md
